name: Benedict XVI
role: Pope of the Roman Catholic Church 2005-2013 (born Joseph Ratzinger, 1927-2022)
summary: Benedict XVI taught that the economy needs ethics and a world authority with real powers, honoured workers' associations, opposed abortion and euthanasia, defined the family as marriage between a man and a woman, and defended a public role for religion while saying the Church cannot replace the State.

unions-good.rationale: Wrote that the Church's calls 'for the promotion of workers' associations that can defend their rights must therefore be honoured today even more than in the past', and criticised governments that limit unions' freedom.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Wrote that outsourcing 'can weaken the company's sense of responsibility towards the stakeholders' and called for 'greater social responsibility on the part of business'.

state-harmful.rationale: Held that 'a just society must be the achievement of politics' and that the Church 'cannot... replace the State', affirming the State's role in justice.

traditional-family.rationale: Called on States to enact 'policies promoting the centrality and the integrity of the family founded on marriage between a man and a woman, the primary vital cell of society'.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Defined the family as 'founded on marriage between a man and a woman' and asked States to promote it as 'the primary vital cell of society'.

abortion-legal.rationale: Condemned governments that 'impose abortion' and 'legislation contrary to life' that spreads 'an anti-birth mentality', and organisations that 'work actively to spread abortion'; 'Openness to life is at the centre of true development'.

more-religion-public.rationale: Told Britain's leaders that the marginalising of religion shows 'a failure to appreciate not only the rights of believers to freedom of conscience and freedom of religion, but also the legitimate role of religion in the public square', urging dialogue between faith and reason 'at every level of national life'.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: At Westminster Hall he voiced concern at 'the increasing marginalization of religion, particularly of Christianity' and at arguments that 'the public celebration of festivals such as Christmas should be discouraged', defending the place of the inherited faith in national life.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Called for 'a reform of the United Nations Organization... so that the concept of the family of nations can acquire real teeth' and 'a true world political authority' that 'would have to have the authority to ensure compliance with its decisions from all parties'.

nation-first.rationale: Said 'no country can be expected to address today's problems of migration by itself' and called for international norms and 'a true world political authority', stressing solidarity between peoples.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: At the UN in 2008 he said that if States cannot protect their people from grave human-rights violations 'the international community must intervene with the juridical means provided in the United Nations Charter', and that 'it is indifference or failure to intervene that do the real damage'.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Wrote that 'the ambiguity of progress becomes evident': it opens 'appalling possibilities for evil', and 'if technical progress is not matched by corresponding progress in man's ethical formation... it is not progress at all, but a threat for man and for the world'.

democracy-best.rationale: At Westminster Hall he listed among shared concerns of the Holy See and the United Kingdom that both 'have welcomed the spread of democracy, especially in the last sixty-five years'; in Berlin he insisted that even the majority is not enough on fundamental questions of law.

separate-church-state.rationale: Wrote that the Church 'cannot and must not replace the State' and that 'a just society must be the achievement of politics, not of the Church', but that she must play her part 'through rational argument'; at Westminster Hall he defended 'the legitimate role of religion in the public square'.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Told the Bundestag that 'Christianity has never proposed a revealed law to the State and to society, that is to say a juridical order derived from revelation. Instead, it has pointed to nature and reason as the true sources of law'.

universal-morality.rationale: Said 'the Catholic tradition maintains that the objective norms governing right action are accessible to reason, prescinding from the content of revelation' and sought the criteria for law in the nature of man.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Described the relation of faith and reason as 'a two-way process': religion 'purifies' reason, and reason purifies religion, neither ranked above the other.

class-collaboration.rationale: Wrote that a business must 'assume responsibility for all the other stakeholders who contribute to the life of the business: the workers, the clients, the suppliers... the community of reference', not only shareholders.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Wrote that 'every migrant is a human person who, as such, possesses fundamental, inalienable rights that must be respected by everyone and in every situation', and that migrant workers are not 'a mere workforce'.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Noted that States face 'limitations to their sovereignty imposed by the new context of international trade and finance', and urged a greater degree of international ordering 'marked by subsidiarity' under a world authority.

clerical-rule.rationale: Wrote that the Church 'cannot and must not take upon herself the political battle to bring about the most just society possible' and 'cannot and must not replace the State'.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Warned that 'cultures are simply placed alongside one another and viewed as substantially equivalent and interchangeable', which 'easily yields to a relativism that does not serve true intercultural dialogue'.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Told the UN that security, development and climate 'require all international leaders to act jointly... promoting solidarity with the weakest regions of the planet', and in Caritas in Veritate called for aid and fair trade for poorer peoples.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Held that the Church's role is to purify reason and form consciences, 'not so much to supply norms... still less to propose concrete political solutions, which would lie altogether outside the competence of religion', yet claimed freedom for the Church to operate publicly; he did not accept State authority over her.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Told the Bundestag, recalling Augustine, 'Without justice - what else is the State but a great band of robbers?' and that 'power became divorced from right' under the Nazis; 'to serve right and to fight against the dominion of wrong is... the fundamental task of the politician'.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Told the Bundestag that for 'the fundamental issues of law, in which the dignity of man and of humanity is at stake, the majority principle is not enough'.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Called on society to review a life-style 'prone to hedonism and consumerism, regardless of their harmful consequences' and for new life-styles in which 'truth, beauty, goodness and communion' determine consumer choices.

non-intervention.rationale: Told the UN that action by the international community 'should never be interpreted as an unwarranted imposition or a limitation of sovereignty. On the contrary, it is indifference or failure to intervene that do the real damage.'

assisted-dying.rationale: Named 'laws permitting euthanasia as well as pressure from lobby groups... in favour of its juridical recognition' as grounds for concern.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Held that for fundamental questions 'everyone in a position of responsibility must personally seek out the criteria to be followed when framing laws', measured against law grounded in nature and reason rather than power.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Observed that in the industrial age 'capital and the means of production were now the new source of power which, concentrated in the hands of a few, led to the suppression of the rights of the working classes'.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Wrote that the State 'which would provide everything, absorbing everything into itself, would ultimately become a mere bureaucracy incapable of guaranteeing the very thing which the suffering person needs: namely, loving personal concern', and that charity will be needed in the most just society.

future-generations.rationale: Wrote of 'our grave duty to hand the earth on to future generations in such a condition that they too can worthily inhabit it', and that creation 'must not be bequeathed to future generations depleted of its resources'.

arms-reduction.rationale: Listed 'integral and timely disarmament' among the tasks requiring a world political authority.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Told the UN that the rights in the Universal Declaration 'apply to everyone by virtue of the common origin of the person' and 'are based on the natural law inscribed on human hearts and present in different cultures and civilizations'.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Cited Origen that a man living under laws contrary to the divine law 'would rightly form associations with like-minded people contrary to the laws', and praised the resistance movements against the Nazi regime for whom 'the law in force was actually unlawful'.

religious-offensive-war.rationale: Quoted with approval Emperor Manuel II's reasoning that 'spreading the faith through violence is something unreasonable. Violence is incompatible with the nature of God and the nature of the soul'.

notes: Read by theme on the Vatican site: Caritas in Veritate, Deus Caritas Est, Spe Salvi, and the Bundestag, Westminster Hall, Regensburg and UN General Assembly addresses. Thirty-seven statements answered, all from his own papal texts (words); acts of governance are not used. The uncertainty rule is not met.
